draft.subject: Tax is not a reason to sell or to wait
draft.english:
Dear [[FIRST_NAME]],

You have told me you would rather wait for your holding to recover than sell it, and I understand why. I only want to make sure one thing is not part of that decision. Across your portfolio there are about USD 1.7m of losses on paper. Because you are taxed in Hong Kong, where there is no tax on capital gains, selling at a loss would not bring any tax benefit, and waiting would not protect one either.

So tax is neither a reason to sell nor a reason to wait. Whether to keep a holding is a question about the holding itself, and about whether it gives you the income you live on.

What I would suggest is that we look at the loss-making positions together, one at a time, in a way you can easily explain to your son.

May I call you this week?
draft.client_language:
[[FIRST_NAME]] 您好：

您曾說過寧願等待該項持倉回升，也不想出售，我明白其中原因。我只是想確保有一件事不會影響這個決定。您的組合目前合計約有 USD 1.7m 的賬面虧損。由於您在香港納稅，而香港不徵收資本增值稅，因此虧本出售不會帶來任何稅務好處，等待也不會保住任何稅務好處。

所以，稅務既不是出售的理由，也不是等待的理由。是否保留某項持倉，取決於該持倉本身，以及它能否為您提供賴以生活的收入。

我的建議是我們一起逐一檢視出現虧損的持倉，並以您能輕鬆向兒子解釋的方式進行。

我可否在本週致電與您詳談？
draft.raises: Asks her to review loss-making positions on their merits, since Hong Kong levies no capital gains tax.
